newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks close higher after seesaw.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks close higher after seesaw.

text.p: Pakistani stocks closed higher on Thursday after dipping at midday and are likely to move up in a narrow range in the next trading week starting after the Friday-Saturday weekend, dealers said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index closed 2.67 points, or 0.18 percent, higher at 1,492.37 after dipping 3.19 points, or 0.21 percent, to 1,486.51 at midday. Advancing stocks led losing ones 145 to 107.
The fall of the PTCL, which carries heavy weightage on the index, eclipsed rises in blue chips, dealer Ali Raza at Kausar Abbas Bhayani said.
Investors are shifting to non-traditional stocks, which is a good sign, and it may help a slow upward movement of the index, Raza said.
ICI gained 1.60 rupees to 21.40, Dewan Salman Fibre 1.20 to 35.40, Dhan Fibres 0.30 to 6.75. PTCL fell 1.15 to 27.55 and Hub Power closed unchanged at 35.15.
